content: 1. During the first week of treatment, mitotane reduces the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of modafinil by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative drug. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of modafinil by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of neratinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of neratinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Coadministration with etravirine may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance to cobicistat. 12. Nevirapine significantly decreases atazanavir exposure, which may lead to loss of therapeutic effect and resistance development. 13. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Coadministration with nevirapine may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance to darunavir. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of norgestimate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) orally twice daily. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of olaparib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) orally twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 30. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) decrease the levels or effects of darunavir by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Coadministration of Viekira Pak with darunavir/ritonavir is not recommended. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 37. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy to avoid potential changes in exposures. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. 38. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 40. Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod through other mechanisms. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
